newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria blasts Belgrade over handling of protests.
newsitem.headline: Austria blasts Belgrade over handling of protests.

text.p: Austria strongly criticised Yugoslavia on Wednesday for its handling of a wave of opposition street protests that have swept the country for over two weeks and urged President Slobodan Milosevic to exercise restraint.
"The situation in Serbia is very emotional and dangerous," Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel said in a statement issued by his office.

"It is unacceptable that Belgrade refuses to accept the outcome of local elections last month," Schuessel said. The poll handed sweeping victories to opposition parties, which were later overturned by Yugoslav courts.
Schuessel called on Milosevic to start a "sensible dialogue" with the opposition and urged him not to resort to violence to quell the mass protests.
"I am warning (Milosevic) not to resort to violent solutions," Schuessel said.
Tens of thousands of people have marched through the streets of Belgrade and other Serbian cities to protest against the annulment of election results and demand Milosevic's removal.
Serbian authorities shut down Radio B-92, one of the country's few independent radio stations, on Tuesday in an apparent attempt to halt its coverage of the demonstrations.
